newsitem.title: USA: Vencor launches $639 million Transitional Hospital offer.
newsitem.headline: Vencor launches $639 million Transitional Hospital offer.

text.p: Vencor Inc., a diversified provider of health care services, said Wednesday it began a cash tender offer to acquire competitor Transitional Hospitals Corp. for $639 million, topping a rival bid for the company.

Vencor's $16-a-share bid is likely to spoil Transitional's agreement announced earlier this week to be acquired by Select Medical Corp. for $14.55 a share in cash. Transitional said at the time it received a $15-per-share offer from an unidentified party after the Select deal was signed.
Analysts said Vencor is likely to emerge as winner in the bidding war.
"Vencor has the better offer and the higher price," said Raymond James analyst John Ransom. "They clearly have the ability to pay more than anybody."
"I don't think Select has the ammo to go higher than $16 and I don't think you'll get a raised bid," said a stock arbitrager who declined to be identified.
Transitional, based in Las Vegas, did not return telephone messages seeking comment and Select, based in Mechanicsburg, Pa., could not immediately comment.
Vencor's stock "is acting like it's a done deal," Ransom said, pointing to the sharp sell-off that usually hits a suitor's stock, amid fears that its earnings would be diluted.
Vencor's stock fell $3.125 to $39.875, while Transitional rose to a $1.125 to $15.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.

The combination of Vencor and Transitional, which operates long-term acute care hospitals, would advance the growth strategy of Vencor, the nation's largest full-service long-term healthcare provider, Vencor said in a statement.

The combined company would have 57 hospitals, 314 skilled nursing centres, 4,000 institutional customers for contract rehabilitation services, 80,000 employees and pro forma annual revenues of $3.3 billion. Vencor said it would retain all of Transitional's non-administrative employees, but did not say how many people might be laid off.

Vencor said it is filing a lawsuit in U.S. District Court in Nevada to invalidate a $19.4 million termination fee called for in the merger agreement between Transitional and Select and will raise its bid by two-thirds of the amount by which the termination fee is reduced if it is successful.

The Vencor offer is scheduled to expire June 4, and is subject to the tender of at least two-thirds of Transitional's fully diluted common shares and equivalents. The offer has no financing contingency.
